subject: Electrical Engineering
title: What Is Electric Current?
description: A 60-second lesson on What Is Electric Current?.

hook.text: Flip a light switch and billions of electrons start marching instantly.

buildup.text: Electrons carry a tiny negative charge. When they move together, that's current.

discovery.text: Current is measured in amperes — one amp equals a coulomb of charge per second.

twist.text: Each electron moves slowly — only millimeters per second through copper wire.

climax.text: The push travels near light speed, but the electrons themselves crawl.

punchline.text: Current is the crowd moving, not any single runner.

quiz.question: What does one ampere of current represent?
options: One electron passing a point per second
One coulomb of charge passing a point per second
One volt of pressure per ohm of resistance
